title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typed page, with handwritten corrections, is not a Grothendieck note on crystals. It is a page of an early typescript of the proper base change theorem in étale cohomology, essentially the material of SGA 4 Exposé XII (Artin, with Grothendieck), filed among the crystal and Dieudonné-module scribbles. The surrounding pages are about (F,V)-structures on triangles and are unrelated.

(1) End of a proof (top half). Setting:
- f: X→S, g: S'→S;
- π: X̄→X with f̄ = fπ (a Chow-type modification), and its base changes π', f', ḡ, g';
- F a torsion sheaf on X, F̄ = π*F, and an injection F̄ ↪ Ḡ chosen so that statement (5.1)(iii), a vanishing of higher direct images, holds for (g, f̄, Ḡ) and for (g', π, Ḡ).

Then R^q f̄'_*(ḡ*Ḡ) ≅ g*(R^q f̄_* Ḡ) and R^q π'_*(ḡ*Ḡ) ≅ g'*(R^q π_* Ḡ) vanish for q>0. The Leray spectral sequence for f̄' = f'π' therefore degenerates and gives R^p f'_*(π'_* ḡ*Ḡ) = 0 for p>0. Since π'_* ḡ*Ḡ ≅ g'*(π_*Ḡ) (degree-0 base change), R^p f'_*(g'*(π_*Ḡ)) = 0 for p>0. Hence π_*F̄ → π_*Ḡ (and so F ↪ π_*Ḡ) is an effacement of the δ-functor (R^p f'_*)∘g'* on torsion sheaves (reference SGA 4 IX 1.1(v)). Effaceability makes the δ-functors universal, so the base change maps are isomorphisms in all degrees by dimension shifting.

(2) Lemma (8.4): it suffices to prove (5.1)(i) (resp. (i)+(ii), resp. (iii)) when f is projective. The proof begins as follows:
- By (6.5), a localisation lemma with P the empty property, one reduces to S strictly local and g the inclusion of the closed point s0.
- One then considers the family of closed subschemes h: Y→X containing the closed fibre X0 such that H^q(X,F) → H^q(X, h_*h*F) is an isomorphism for every F and every relevant q.
- This is the start of a Noetherian-induction / limit argument combined with Chow's lemma.

All of this is the standard proof of proper base change (Artin, SGA 4 XII; also Deligne's SGA 4½ Arcata), and serves that theorem.
errors: In the conclusion of the Leray argument the condition is written 'pour q>0'; it should be p>0, both for R^p f'_*(π'_* ḡ*Ḡ) = 0 and for R^p f'_*(g'*(π_*Ḡ)) = 0.
The notation drifts between f̄' and f' in the spectral sequence. The abutment R^n f̄'_*(Ḡ) should read R^n f̄'_*(ḡ*Ḡ). These are typographical slips, not mathematical gaps.

ideas.what: Effacement argument: an injection into a sheaf whose higher direct images vanish universally makes (R^p f'_*)g'* effaceable, giving base change in all degrees.
ideas.modern_name: Universal δ-functors / effaceability in the proof of proper base change
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Tôhoku) for effaceability; Artin for proper base change (SGA 4 XII)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. XII (Artin), using SGA 4 IX

ideas.what: Reduction of proper base change to projective f, and to S strictly local with g the closed point.
ideas.modern_name: Chow's lemma reduction plus strict localisation in proper base change

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of the well-known SGA 4 XII proof of proper base change, misfiled among the crystal notes. Its only interest is archival: earlier numbering (Lemme 8.4) and handwritten editorial corrections.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed, with handwritten corrections: 'résulte' replaces 's'ensuite', and 'pertinent,' replaces 'applicable'.
'pour q>0' after R^p f'_*(...) is a typo in the original for p>0; the transcription is faithful to it.
The reference reads '(IX 1.1 (v))', apparently handwritten over a struck word.
The struck word before 'effacement' is illegible.
